page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache allocation includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware acceleration for AES encryption.

Hardware capacity is weighted toward memory, delivering 32.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The configuration includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage disks such as Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include GPU acceleration hardware, nor does it include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight that the compute capacity falls largely within lower tiers across multi-threaded metrics. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 4,380.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,867.0, both positioning in the bottom 25% of measured systems. In contrast, single-threaded metrics show more balanced outcomes: Geekbench single-core reached 1,290.0, gzip compression recorded 23.87 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression achieved 9.35 GB/sec, all landing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show 27.89 GB/sec read and 21.97 GB/sec write throughput for large blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4s_v4 prioritizes a high memory footprint over raw multi-core compute density. Workloads that do not require high parallel throughput or dedicated local scratch storage can leverage the 1:8 core-to-memory ratio efficiently. The instance is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, medium-sized in-memory caches, relational database systems relying on network block storage, and general mid-tier application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure E4s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon 8272CL processor, featuring 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance carries no bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware. Performance metrics demonstrate moderate single-threaded capability alongside lower multi-core performance tiers, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,290.0 and a multi-core score of 2,867.0. Given its high RAM-to-vCPU ratio and reliance on external persistent storage, the E4s_v4 is suited for in-memory caching systems, small-to-medium relational databases, and enterprise backends that demand substantial memory capacity without heavy parallel processing requirements.
